Awareness & solutions

How We Can Keep Traditions Alive

You don't need to be an expert. Small steps, taken by many people, make a big difference.

Start with one small step

  1. 01

    Learn a skill

    Pick one tradition and try it, even just once.

    Explore skills
  2. 02

    Buy handmade

    When your family buys a gift, choose something made by an artisan.

  3. 03

    Ask your elders

    Ask grandparents what songs, foods or crafts they grew up with. Write it down!

  4. 04

    Share the stories

    Tell your friends or class about a tradition you discovered.

  5. 05

    Celebrate the days

    Mark National Handloom Day on 7 August by wearing or learning about handloom.

  6. 06

    Take the quiz

    Not sure where to start? Find your match in 30 seconds.

    Take the quiz

How groups can help

  • Schools

    Invite artisans for a talk or demonstration, and plan trips to craft museums.

  • Communities

    Hold craft fairs and festivals where artisans can sell directly to buyers.

  • Organisations

    Run workshops, record skills on video, and help artisans reach new markets.

Useful links & resources

These links go to other websites and open in a new tab. You're leaving Sanskriti, so check with a parent, guardian or teacher.

  • SPIC MACAY

    A youth movement that brings classical music, dance and crafts to schools and colleges.

  • Crafts Council of India

    Supports artisans and runs craft bazaars and shops.

  • People's Archive of Rural India

    Stories and photos about the lives and work of rural India, including artisans.

  • Kalakshetra Foundation

    A school of dance, music and arts in Chennai, founded in 1936.

  • UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage

    India's living traditions recognised by UNESCO.

  • Development Commissioner (Handlooms)

    The Government of India office that supports handloom weavers.
